title: A Standardized Open Scheming Benchmark for Open-Weight Models

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a standardized benchmark enables reproducible comparison of scheming behaviors across models and labs. Without this, the field cannot track progress or compare results systematically.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: designing scheming scenarios requires understanding of the field, but implementation (prompts, scoring scripts, model runs) is manageable. Running on 5 models adds compute overhead.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Broad scope: designing 20-30 scenarios with scoring rubrics, building leaderboard infrastructure, running on 5 models, and releasing code is a substantial project well beyond 30 hours for beginners.

evidence: Petri and Petri 2.0 (Anthropic 2025-2026) provide an open-source standardized framework for testing scheming behaviors across models with scoring rubrics.
MALT (METR 2025) provides 10,919 transcripts for evaluation tampering detection with standardized scoring.
DeceptionBench (PKU-Alignment 2025) offers 150 scenarios including sandbagging and strategic deception evaluation.
Apollo Research scheming evals provide reproducible protocols tested across frontier models.
Multiple standardized benchmarks for scheming/deception already exist, though no single unified 'scheming leaderboard' for open-weight models has been established.
